title: Proposition 4.2: degree-dependent lower bound for weighted spectral approximation of the complete graph
statement_scope: Whole Proposition pro:lowerComplete: Let G be the complete graph on vertex set V, and let H=(V,E,w) be a weighted graph with n vertices and a vertex of degree d. If H kappa-approximates G, then kappa >= 1 + 2/sqrt(d) - O(sqrt(d)/n). The displayed asymptotic O(sqrt(d)/n) bound and the author's degree-d vertex hypothesis are retained without strengthening, boundary repair, or added assumptions.

standard_prerequisites: Spectral kappa-approximation: for all x, x^T L_G x <= x^T L_H x <= kappa x^T L_G x; and x^T L_G x = sum_{(u,v) in E} w_{u,v}(x_u-x_v)^2 (journal.tex 145-166).

Rayleigh quotient/eigenvalue comparison and orthogonal projection onto the all-ones orthogonal complement in R^n.

difficulty_reason: OwnH2: construct opposite-sign witnesses on one degree-d star, compare their exact weighted Laplacian forms under kappa-approximation, project both orthogonally to constants and retain the finite-n norm-ratio error to force the asymptotic lower bound. It is a lower-bound witness construction for irregular weighted graphs, distinct from sparse-weight existence and common-barrier feasibility. The given Rayleigh principle alone does not choose these witnesses or control the unequal projection losses; H2 is tied to those explicit author steps, not the named graph problem.

semantic_comparisons.comparison: Public 900009463 is Theorem 3.1 (thm:linalg): a sparse nonnegative identity-frame decomposition with an exact two-sided Loewner bound at 351-362. The new unit is a lower bound on kappa for any weighted graph kappa-approximating a complete graph using a degree-d vertex at 1043-1054. The quantified objects, hypotheses, conclusions and proofs differ: identity-frame vectors and an iterative barrier construction versus a complete graph, a weighted graph, star test vectors and an asymptotic lower bound.

Public 900009465 is Lemma 3.5 (lem:shiftboth): a rank-one update preserving both spectral barriers under the hypotheses at 739-756. The new proposition has no barrier potentials, no both-barrier condition and no rank-one update; it proves a Laplacian kappa-approximation lower bound using two opposite-sign star test vectors and projection errors at 1057-1197. Not the same result.
